f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y),\, & \text{if}\,0<x<\pi ,\,-\frac{\pi }{2}<y<0, \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(x-y),\, & \text{if}\,0<x<\pi ,\,0<y<\frac{\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Then,

$$
{∬}_{(0,\pi )\times (-\pi /2,\pi /2)}f(x,y)\text{ }\text{d}A=
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that the rectangle $R$ can be represented as a union of two smaller rectangles, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}R & =(0,\pi )\times ((-\frac{\pi }{2},0)\cup (0,\frac{\pi }{2})) \\  & =((0,\pi )\times (-\frac{\pi }{2},0))\cup ((0,\pi )\times (0,\frac{\pi }{2})).\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A & ={∬}_{(0,\pi )\times (-\pi /2,0)}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A+{∬}_{(0,\pi )\times (0,\pi /2)}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{(0,\pi )\times (-\pi /2,0)}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)\,\text{d}A+{∬}_{(0,\pi )\times (0,\pi /2)}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-y)\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
Using the linearity property of double integrals, we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}(3{x}^{2}+6{y}^{2})\text{d}A & ={∬}_{R}3{x}^{2}\text{ }\text{d}A+{∬}_{R}6{y}^{2}\text{ }\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

The function under the first integral is independent of $y.$ So, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}3{x}^{2}\text{ }\text{d}A & =(2-0){\int }_{-1}^{0}3{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2({x}^{3}{|}_{-1}^{0}) \\  & =2({0}^{3}-(-1)^{3}) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

The function under the second integral is independent of $x.$ So, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}6{y}^{2}\text{ }\text{d}A & =(0-(-1)){\int }_{0}^{2}6{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =2{y}^{3}{|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =2\cdot {2}^{3}-0 \\  & =16.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, combining our results, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}(3{x}^{2}+6{y}^{2})\,\text{d}A=2+16=18.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given that $C$ and $D$ are finite, non-overlapping regions and that

$$
{∬}_{C}f(x,y)\text{ }\text{d}A=-5,\,{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\text{ }\text{d}A=-10,
$$

find the value of 

$$
{∬}_{C\cup D}2f(x,y)\text{ }\text{d}A.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Using the linearity and additivity of double integrals, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{C\cup D}2f(x,y)\text{ }\text{d}A & =2{∬}_{C\cup D}f(x,y)\text{ }\text{d}A \\  & =2({∬}_{C}f(x,y)\text{ }\text{d}A+{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\text{ }\text{d}A) \\  & =2(-5-10) \\  & =-30\end{aligned}
$$
